title.narrative: Number of annual land transactions registered, excluding first time registration (disaggregated by transfers, mortgages, leases and inheritance; disaggregated by gender)

comment.narrative:
The indicator measures the annual number of subsequent land transactions in Lao PDR. The data is disaggregated by transfer, mortgages, leases and inheritance. The disaggregated information will eventually be available directly from Lao LandReg but for now is conducted manually via reviewing logbooks at each of the 18 PONRE offices. The baseline data is based on 2019 information from all provinces, except Phongsaly, Luangnamtha, Khammouane and Salavan due to lack of data provided to central level.
From January to December 2024, there were a total of 39,427 transactions, which includes 19,808 sales, 12,594 mortgages, 1,925 inheritances, 5,011 transfers and 89 leases out of which 58.36% were in the name of women. The majority of provinces reported increases in land transactions; however, the decrease in transfers was caused by substantial drops in transactions reported by two large provinces-Vientiane Capital City and Luang Prabang.

comment.narrative:
The indicator measures the annual number of subsequent land transactions in Lao PDR. The data is disaggregated by transfer, mortgages, leases and inheritance. The disaggregated information will eventually be available directly from Lao LandReg but for now is conducted manually via reviewing logbooks at each of the 18 PONRE offices. The baseline data is based on 2019 information from all provinces, except Phongsaly, Luangnamtha, Khammouane and Salavan due to lack of data provided to central level.
DOL provided the annual transaction data for 2022 and 2023. For the year 2022, there were a total of 35,974 transactions including 22,129 sales, 6,752 mortgages, 4,999 transfers, 2,042 inheritances and 52 leases. Transactions in the name of females was 43.08% for 2022. For 2023, there were a total of 50,296 subsequent land transactions, including 34,965 sales,11,052 mortgages, 1,845 transfers, 2413 inheritances, and 21 leases out of which 51.95% were in the name of women.

title.narrative: Beneficiaries who participate in public awareness campaigns (disaggregated by ethnicity)

comment.narrative:
This indicator measures the percentage of beneficiaries participating the project public awareness campaigns out of the total number of households, as well as provides the percentage that are ethnic. This indicator was restructured in February 2024. Baseline was set to 0 instead of 50% as public awareness campaigns for ESLRP began in 2023. The indicator was revised to 33.3 % instead of 50% to reflect that often only 1 person per extended family (multiple households) attends the public awareness campaigns.
48,287 individuals have attended public awareness campaigns reaching 40.4% of the 119,583 households across 605 villages. Of all participants, 12,128 were from ethnic minority groups, accounting for 25.1% of overall attendance.

title.narrative: Average cost of issuance of new land title

comment.narrative:
This indicator measures the average cost of issuing a new land title. Baseline was set at 25 dollars based on a GIZ study. This analysis covers costs related to investments, training, and daily operations.
By December 2024, a strong increase in the number of issued land titles led to a significant reduction in cost, bringing the average down to $30.80 per issued land title.

title.narrative: Average cost of issuance of new land title

comment.narrative: This indicator measures the average cost of issuing a new land title. Baseline was set at 25 dollars based on a GIZ study. A detailed analysis of the cost per plot was conducted in September 2024, using a similar methodology to GIZ. This analysis covers costs related to investments, training, and daily operations. According to this approach, the current cost per land title stands at $66.40, while the average cost per surveyed land plot stands at $25.72. Projections indicate that as the project reaches a milestone of at least 500,000 plots titled, the cost is expected to drop below $18.00 per parcel.

title.narrative: Income generation to government through DOL (excluding first registration fees) in Lao Kip

comment.narrative:
This indicator measures amount of annual income generated to the government by DOL through land administration fees excluding first-time registration fees. It was restructured in February 2024 from US$ to Kip due to the drastic change in exchange rate (from 9,170 at baseline to over 20,000), as well as removing the LAK 747,362,000 out of LAK 779,492,650 million from the baseline which was capital gains tax and hence not DOL income. Baseline was hence reset to LAK32,131,000 to count only DOL income.
As this is annual indicator, next reporting will be March 2025 covering calendar year 2024. 2022 income was LAK 56,715,639 while 2023 income was LAK 38,896,339.

title.narrative: Land titles or use certificates issued by the project in selected areas (disaggregated by titles/certificates, gender and ethnicity)

comment.narrative:
This indicator will measure the number of properties and land parcels in Lao PDR that have received land title or use certificate. Land titles and use certificates are considered to be issued when they are prepared and printed, regardless if the land holder collects them from DONRE or not. The disaggregated information will be reported in the progress reports. The disaggregated information on titles/certificates and gender is available in Lao LandReg, while disaggregated information on ethnicity must be collected through other means, such as reports of the mobile units or DONREs. The ethnicity information is not expected to be collected in the first year of project implementation.
As of December 2024, 71% of titles have been issued to women, including to women only, conjugal and joint titles, while 17% of titles have been issued to ethnic group people.

title.narrative: Coverage of cadastral index maps showing all land holdings, including communal lands, prepared by the project in selected areas.

comment.narrative:
This indicator shows the coverage of the cadastral index maps prepared in the project. Communal land refers to state land for collective use. In the February 2024 restructuring, this indicator was revised to only include hectares mapped by the Project. Accordingly the endline target was reset to 1,484,517 ha.
Based on September 2024 data in the central Lao LandReg database, the average plot size in ESLRP target areas was 1.19 hectares (comprising around 2/3 agriculture land use and 1/3 construction land). With a total of 177,248 surveyed land plots, the total coverage of cadastral index maps computes to 210,225 hectares.

title.narrative: Coverage of cadastral index maps showing all land holdings, including communal lands, prepared by the project in selected areas.

title.narrative: Land titles or use certificates issued by the project in selected areas (disaggregated by titles/certificates, gender and ethnicity)

comment.narrative:
This indicator will measure the number of properties and land parcels in Lao PDR that have received land title or use certificate by ESLRP. Land titles and use certificates are considered to be issued when they are prepared and printed. The indicator was revised during restructuring in February 2024 to capture solely titles issued by the project and not all land titles issued by GoL. Accordingly the baseline was reset to 0 and the target was revised to 650,000. Disaggregated data on gender includes titles issued in the name of women/conjugal/joint.
As of end of September 2024, 80,549 titles had been issued across 32 districts. Based on available disaggregated data, 70% have been issued to women. When applied to the total, this means approximately 56,534 titles have been issued to women. 12, 642 land titles (21%) have been issued to landowners from ethnic minority groups.

title.narrative: Customer satisfaction with land administration services in selected offices (disaggregated by gender)

comment.narrative: This indicator measures the percentage of customers satisfied with land administration services in selected offices. The indicator was revised in restructuring in February 2024 to calculate the baseline and endline as percentages rather than on a scale of 1 to 5 and include both primary and subsequent land transactions. The baseline survey found overall 62 percent customer satisfaction in land services (67.5 percent satisfaction for males and 57.3 percent for females), including those carrying out first registration and subsequent transactions. For first time registration, 56 percent of customers were satisfied and 70 percent of the respondents (504/720) were satisfied or very satisfied when conducting secondary transactions. An endline customer satisfaction survey is planned by project completion.
